# Smoke test for the Triangle vocabulary and checker.
#
# Four made-up product stories written out as commit subjects. Together they use every
# entry of the vocabulary. Every line that is not a comment must pass `gitmoji check`
# with the default settings.
# A comment starting with `# hard:` marks the line above it as one where tagging was a
# judgement. Lines starting with `##` are phases of a story.
#
# The tags are one author's choices. They are a test of the tool, not a reference for
# how each line should be tagged.

### Story 1: a zoo guide, from pipeline to product

## Data engineers: dbt and Dagster
🗃️🏗️ #501 (pipelines): set up the dbt project and the Dagster code location
🗃️➕ #501 (pipelines): add dbt and Dagster
🛰️🔌 #501 (pipelines): load gate scans from the ticketing system
🗃️🧮 #501 (pipelines): clean gate scans into one row per scan
🗃️👔 #501 (pipelines): count a visit when a scan is followed by 30 seconds at an enclosure
🗃️🧮 #501 (pipelines): build one row per visit and enclosure
🗃️🏷️ #501 (pipelines): publish the columns and types of the visits table
🗃️🛡️ #501 (pipelines): stop the run when a visit has no enclosure
🗃️⛓️ #501 (pipelines): rebuild visits every night after the gates close
🗃️🥅 #501 (pipelines): retry the gate load three times
🗃️🔊 #501 (pipelines): report how fresh the visits table is
🧱🔧 #501 (infra): give the nightly run four workers
## Data scientists: a trial in marimo notebooks
🧠🆕🧪 #510 (notebooks): add a notebook that answers questions from the visits table
🧠🎭🧪 #510 (notebooks): add sixty sample visitor questions
🧠🎯🧪 #510 (notebooks): score answers by whether they name the right enclosure
🧠🐛🧪 #510 (notebooks): keep closed enclosures out of the answers
🧠🔧🧪 #510 (notebooks): try a lower temperature for Arctic questions
🧠📊🧪 #510 (notebooks): record the scores per zoo section
🧠🏁 #510 (notebooks): keep section-aware answers and move them into the api
👷🔌 #510 (ci): run the answer scoring on every pull request
🧠🕹️ #512 (notebooks): publish the notebook as a page for trying questions without the app
🧠📊 #512 (ci): add a PDF of the answer scores to every merge
## Into the product: Expo app and api
🧩🏷️ #520 (api): define the question and answer types for the zoo guide
🧠🆕 #520 (api): add the zoo guide that answers from visits
🧠🛡️ #520 (api): refuse questions that are not about the zoo
🧠🔧 #520 (api): set the temperature per zoo section
🧩🔌 #520 (api): expose the askGuide endpoint
🧩🔌 #520 (api): expose the per-section guide configuration
🧩🎚️ #520 (api): put the zoo guide behind a switch
🎨🚸 #520 (app): ask the guide from an enclosure page
🎨🥅 #520 (app): say so when the guide cannot answer
🎨💫 #520 (app): let the answer unfold as it arrives
🎨💬 #520 (app): greet visitors by the section they are in
🎨🚸 #520 (app): read answers aloud with the screen reader
🎨✨ #520 (app): let visitors ask the zoo guide
🧩🚀 #520 (api): open the guide to season-ticket holders
## A new model arrives: Mastra and compiled prompts
🧠➕🧪 #530 (prompts): add Mastra to compile prompts
🧠🎭🧪 #530 (evals): add 200 visitor questions with expected answers
🧠⛓️🧪 #530 (prompts): compile prompts against the evaluation set
🧠🏁 #530 (prompts): keep compiled prompts as the way prompts are made
🧠⬆️ #531 (api): move the guide to the new model
# hard: Still a judgement. 👽️ if the old model was switched off: the line is whether we moved or the outside did.
🧠👽️ #531 (api): stop the new model padding tropical answers
🧠📥 #531 (prompts): take over prompts compiled for the new model in run 87
# hard: Still a judgement. 📦️ if the compile only used sources in this repo. A model call is not repeatable, so 📥 with a Source: line.
## Fitting the guide: ordinary work, no third emoji
🧠🎯 #532 (evals): count a wrong enclosure twice as heavily as a vague answer
🧠🔧 #532 (api): raise the Arctic temperature for the new model
🧠📊 #532 (evals): record the scores of the new prompts per zoo section
🧠🎭 #532 (evals): add forty questions about night-time enclosures
🧠🎯 #532 (evals): score answers per section, not overall

### Story 2: the whole lifecycle, ending with a baseball cap

## Adopting the convention
🔺 gitmoji `2.0.0`: pairs replace single emojis
## Platform: Azure, Kubernetes, secrets
🧱🆕 #601 (infra): describe the Azure resource group and the cluster as code
🧱🛂 #601 (infra): let the deploy identity pull images and nothing else
🧱🔐 #601 (infra): keep the database password in the key vault
🧱🔧 #601 (infra): run three api pods in production and one in staging
🧱🔊 #601 (infra): alert when a pod restarts more than twice an hour
## Workbench: dev container, task files, agents
🧑‍💻🆕 #602 (devcontainer): add a dev container that needs only Docker
🧑‍💻🎭 #602 (devcontainer): start the dev container with synthetic visits loaded
🧑‍💻☑️ #602 (ci): check in the pipeline that a breakpoint can be set in VS Code
🧑‍💻🆕 #603 (tasks): add task files that run any package locally
🧑‍💻📱 #603 (tasks): run the app on a plugged-in Android phone or iPhone with one task
🤖🆕 #604 (toolbelt): add a script that lists the packages a change touches
🤖📝 #604 (agents): tell agents to reach for the toolbelt before writing a script
🤖♻️ #605 (agents): split the root instructions into one short entry per package
🧩📝 #605 (docs): explain how the packages fit together
## Switches, policies, entitlements
🧩🎚️ #610 (api): add a switch each for creating, reading, changing and deleting cards
🧩➕ #610 (api): add Cerbos
🧩🛂 #610 (policies): let only a card's owner trade it
🧩🛂 #610 (policies): give season-ticket holders the premium card set
🎨🎚️🧪 #611 (app): show half of visitors the new card layout
🧩🔊🧪 #611 (api): count trades per card layout
🎨📊🧪 #611 (app): record that the new layout led to more trades
🎨🏁 #611 (app): keep the new card layout and remove its switch
# hard: A limit that stays. The closer now names its evidence, the 📊 above. But a switch flipped in the flag service leaves no commit unless its state is mirrored into the repository.
🧩🔧 #612 (api): declare the map key in the env schema
🧩👔 #613 (pricing): apply Germany's reduced VAT rate to tickets
🧩👔 #614 (api): keep card trading off where the law forbids it
# hard: 👔, 🎚️ or 🔧? Ask who turns it. The law decides, so it is a rule. If product could turn it per country it would be 🎚️; if engineers set it per deployment, 🔧.

# hard: 🎨 is tempting because it runs on the phone. The area is the side of the coin, not the device: this is capability, and the scope says where it runs.
🧩🆕 #624 (ledger): add the trade ledger as a Rust module for the edge worker

🧩☑️ #720 (errors): fail the build when an error carries an uncatalogued code

🎨🌐 #720 (i18n): add German error descriptions

# hard: 🥅 or 🔌 for returning the code with a failed request. It changes what happens after a failure, so 🥅.
